bullets.title: S&P 500 hits new ATH at 7,800 on soft PPI; Fed hike odds fall to 31%
bullets.body: Two consecutive days of below-expected inflation data (core PCE 3M annualized at 1.64%, down from 2.29%) pushed the S&P 500 to its 27th all-time high of 2026, crossing 7,800 for the first time. Market pricing for a September Fed rate hike fell to 31%, with MS, JPM, and 22V all expecting the Fed on hold through year-end. However, Piper Sandler warns core PCE diffusion indices signal sticky inflation, and commodity-driven CPI expected to stay above 3% YoY in August.

bullets.title: 30-year Treasury auction clears at 5.22%—highest since 2001; real yields at decade highs
bullets.body: The $25B 30-year bond auction cleared at 5.22%, highest since August 2001, as AI infrastructure debt issuance and fiscal deficits ($432B federal deficit in July alone) combine with elevated supply. US national debt up $3.7T in 13 months. Morgan Stanley's UST 7s30s steepeners offer 'highest vol-adjusted carry since mid-2022'; Fed trough funds priced at 3.94%.

bullets.title: BOJ September rate hike probability surges to ~81%; yen consolidating
bullets.body: Reuters and multiple sell-side sources report the Bank of Japan is eyeing a September rate hike with OIS pricing at ~81% probability vs ~65% the prior Friday. A former Japanese FX official warns of increased yen intervention potential and faster tightening pace. JPY bulls cautious below 159.50 (50% Fibonacci level); British pound approaching 1.35 as Fed hike bets ease.

bullets.title: Oil volatile: Hormuz tanker attacks spike crude 2%+ early before settling lower
bullets.body: Iran's IRGC Navy Commander claimed the Strait of Hormuz closed; two UAE ADNOC tankers were attacked in the strait. WTI surged to $82.99 intraday before settling down 2.4% at $81.25; Brent fell 2.2% to $87.07. US Energy Secretary Wright says 8-9M barrels transit Hormuz daily and the US will continue escort operations; Treasury Secretary Bessent threatened 'unprecedented' Iran sanctions. Diesel cracks hit new all-time highs after Houthi attacks on Saudi Aramco.

bullets.title: Tech sector breaking out: Nasdaq 100 on track for 2nd-best August this century
bullets.body: The Nasdaq 100 is on pace for its second-best August performance this century, with 73% of constituents trading above their 200-day moving average—strongest breadth in 13 months. Hedge funds net bought 4.5% US equity GMV since early August via short covering and AI name buying; semis saw +2.5 standard deviation HF buying. Equal-weight S&P 500 also breaking out technically. Mag7/MegaCap Tech still trading >2 standard deviations below 2018-present mean on forward P/E, implying ~30-56% upside to historical averages per JPM.

bullets.title: WDAY Silver Lake take-private at ~$50B EV lifts SaaS sector; validates systems-of-record floor
bullets.body: Reuters reported Silver Lake is in talks to acquire Workday for $50B+ EV (~$230-240/share, 30% premium), potentially the largest software buyout ever. The news drove the GS TMT SaaS basket sharply higher, IGV up 3%, and broad re-rating of SaaS multiples (up 8%+ WoW). Jefferies and UBS both raised WDAY targets. Multiple sources call this a 'valuation floor' signal for software given private equity interest validating AI de-rating as excessive; Wolfe All-SaaS index at 5.7x FY+2 EV/Sales.

bullets.title: OpenAI ARR tops $40B (doubled from YE25); AI pricing wars intensify with Chinese rivals
bullets.body: OpenAI's annualized revenue exceeded $40B in July, up 20%+ month-over-month and double year-end 2025 levels, driven by AI coding software and advertising. Anthropic tracking toward $47B ARR (IPO at ~$2T valuation cited by Polymarket at 53-60% probability). Simultaneously, a pricing war is accelerating: OpenAI and Anthropic cutting token prices against Chinese open-weight alternatives; DeepSeek raised V4 Pro prices 4x but blended costs remain lower than peers.

bullets.title: NVIDIA $500B AI financing platform with Apollo/BlackRock/GS shifts AI capex funding model
bullets.body: NVIDIA established $500B+ compute financing partnerships with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR—capable of supporting 12-14GW of AI infrastructure capacity. GPU-backed financing deals use power as collateral; Bloomberg reports deals could hit market in 'tens of billions at a time.' AMD simultaneously raised $4.75B in its largest-ever bond offering. YTD TMT debt issuance at $331B; AI infrastructure funding increasingly shifting to private credit and asset-backed structures.

bullets.title: NVIDIA neocloud revenue-sharing model seen driving $37B+ incremental revenue at scale
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Joe Moore models NVIDIA receiving 35% of GPU rental price spread above backstop from neocloud deployments—implying ~$7.4B annual revenue per GW of capacity and ~$37B incremental revenue at 5GW (7% FY29 EPS upside). UBS and MS both raised NVDA estimates: UBS models FQ2 beat of $3-4B (~$94-95B revenue), FQ3 guidance ~$107-108B, C2027 EPS path to $15+. PT range: $280 (UBS Buy), $288 (MS Bull), $330 bull case. Feynman next-gen GPU ahead of schedule on TSMC A16, targeting H2 2028.

bullets.title: NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics enters full production; supply chain: TSM, LITE, COHR
bullets.body: NVIDIA announced its Spectrum-X Ethernet photonics scale-out networking infrastructure is now in full production. TSM provides silicon photonics fab via COUPE process; Lumentum (LITE) supplies ELS, high-power lasers, and optical alignment/test; Coherent (COHR) supplies ELS and optical components; Fabrinet (FN) handles switch CPO assembly and test; GLW provides fiber and connectors. Meta's 50M-hour study confirms CPO reliability is higher than pluggable optics with zero link flap observed.

bullets.title: SNDK Investor Day: 80% gross margins, 100% FCF return, HBF as AI inference wildcard
bullets.body: SanDisk's Investor Day set FY28-30 targets of mid-to-high teens revenue growth, ~80% gross margin, ~75% operating margin, and ~50% FCF—with 100% of excess FCF returned to shareholders. Multi-year NBM contracts now cover ~50% of bits in FY26 rising to ~66-70% by FY29, replacing quarterly transactional negotiations with 4-year visibility. HBF (High Bandwidth Flash) samples expected in 2027, targeting 8-16x larger capacity at comparable cost. Global flash market projected to reach $300B in 2026 and $500B in 2027. JPMorgan resumed at Overweight; Citi reiterates Buy at $2,100 PT; Mizuho raised to $1,900; GS raised PT to $2,200.

bullets.title: RDDT joins S&P 500 Aug 18: 12.8M shares of net indexer demand (~211% of daily volume)
bullets.body: Reddit replaces AvalonBay Communities in the S&P 500 effective before the open on August 18. JPMorgan estimates net indexer demand of 12.8M shares, representing 211% of average daily volume—the second pure-play social media company in the index. RDDT traded up 10.6-12% pre-market. Separately, Reddit's average users fell 2% in July vs June but July momentum improved into August; July ad spend growth 130bps above expectations per Piper.

bullets.title: Fitch affirms US at AA+ stable; fiscal trajectory sees Medicare/SS up ~1ppt GDP by 2032
bullets.body: Fitch affirmed the United States at AA+ with a stable outlook, citing large economy, high per-capita income, and exceptional financing flexibility. Downside risks include Medicare and Social Security costs expanding by ~1pp of GDP by 2032, increasing gridlock/shutdown probability, and elevated deficit spending. Fitch forecasts US GDP growth at 1.9% in 2026-2027, down from 2.8% in 2025, with inflation toward target by year-end 2028.

bullets.title: Trump imposes up to 100% tariff on drones; 15% on Taiwan/EU/Japan, 10% on UK
bullets.body: Trump signed a proclamation imposing 100% ad valorem tariffs on sensitive drones and 25% on smaller drones, with a 15% tariff on drones and components from EU, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, Taiwan, and Liechtenstein, and 10% on UK. Tariffs take effect in 21 days; non-sensitive components in 180 days. White House separately reports $19-26B in annual tariff revenue lost to transshipment/'Great China Transshipment Scam.' Domestic solar producers (FSLR) seen as beneficiaries of parallel poly 232 framework.

bullets.title: AI margin premium widens: AI-using S&P companies showing higher NTM margin than non-AI peers
bullets.body: 22V Research finds NTM margin estimates for AI Users are outpacing non-AI Users in both level and rate of change through 2Q, with the advantage highest in Tech and Communication Services but also present in Financials, Utilities, Discretionary, and Industrials. Hyperscalers likely to generate attractive ROI on AI capex investments, supporting continued spend. 22V favors both AI goods (semis, AI power) and AI services simultaneously, alongside long cyclicals and short defensives/low earnings vol names.

bullets.title: FRBNY pauses reserve management purchases Aug 14–Sept 14; first pause since QT ended
bullets.body: Piper Sandler notes the NY Fed's reserve management purchase program was paused for August 14–September 14, the first pause since QT ended in late 2025, conducting only $17B in reinvestment purchases. Separately, FRBNY confirms the FIMA repo facility remains untouched despite rising foreign cash reserves. Atlanta Fed Wage Tracker ticked up from 3.6% to 3.8% in July, assessed as 'very slightly hawkish' but offset by benign goods/services price data.

bullets.title: Data center political risk rising: power bills driving consumer opposition to AI buildout
bullets.body: Roth QSG is surveying 750-1,250 US adults in PJM/ERCOT regions to quantify electricity bill inflation, blame attribution, and local support for AI data centers. Rising electricity costs are turning into political resistance that may slow data center approvals. Texas and New York data center moratoriums viewed as 'temporary/political' by JPM. Europe faces power crisis from heat waves/drought with France/Germany peak prices at €300/MWh; Romania shut its sole nuclear plant.

bullets.title: Russia-Ukraine war: Black Sea emerging as dangerous corridor threatening grain/oil inflation
bullets.body: JPM's Russia-Ukraine update warns the war is likely to persist through 2027 with static frontlines. Ukraine successfully targeted Russian oil shipping in the Black Sea; Russia retaliates against Ukrainian ports, potentially blocking 30M tons of agricultural exports. Ukraine faces acute Patriot missile shortages. Russia expected to escalate hybrid attacks on European infrastructure in H2 2026–2027. Black Sea disruption could create 'upward inflationary pressures on global grain and oil markets.'

bullets.title: US real yields at decade highs; hyperscaler borrowing binge reshaping foreign credit markets
bullets.body: Real yields across major economies hit decade highs as AI capex-driven debt issuance surges alongside government deficits. The FT reports hyperscalers' AI infrastructure debt issuance is reshaping foreign credit markets. JULI credit index widened 1.4bps. Taiwan raised its 2026 GDP forecast to 11.05% on AI-driven chip hub outperformance. South Korea ICT exports surged 140% in July on AI chip demand.

bullets.title: Retail Sales preview: JPM Feroli expects -0.4% MoM; control group -0.3% from Prime Day shift
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Feroli projects July Retail Sales at -0.4% MoM vs +0.1% survey consensus, driven by lower gasoline prices, vehicle dealers, and auto sales. The control group is expected at -0.3% vs +0.3% survey due to Amazon Prime Day timing shift and unwinding of tax stimulus. Upcoming retail earnings (Home Depot Tuesday, Lowes/TJX/Target Wednesday, Ross/Walmart Thursday) will provide next major read on consumer health. G-4 saving rates have fallen 1.6pp since end-2024 as wealth effects cushion weak income growth.
